items.reading_mnemonic: One shrine cat, nicknamed <reading>Shii</reading> for the hiss she makes mid-gnaw, clamps onto the bell rim and hisses <reading>し</reading> through the gap where a tooth used to be.

items.meaning_mnemonic: At the riverbank a <radical>drop</radical> slides off a leaf, frozen mid-fall. A fisherman's line snaps into the hook of <radical>nine</radical>, yanking tight around it and reeling it in, coiling around and around until it's squeezed into one tight ball. That coiled sphere, drawn shut on itself, is round.
items.reading_mnemonic: The fisherman reeling in that tight round ball grunts <reading>がん</reading> with every heave, a sound as sharp as a rusty <reading>gun</reading> cocking twice. Neighbors on the riverbank swear they can hear it from their porches.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Toto the door-to-door turtle sets up shop outside Koichi's konbini, hauling a sample <radical>door</radical> off his shell. Its top panel keeps swinging open on its own, scraping against the sill with every gust. He pitches it as a feature: it never latches, so you're never locked out again. Nobody wants that.
items.reading_mnemonic: Outside that same konbini, Toto scrapes his shell along the loose sill trying to force a sale, and each scrape knocks out the same hollow sound: <reading>coh</reading>, <reading>こ</reading>. Shoppers wince every time but can't stop hearing it after they've left. Toto just shrugs it off as free advertising.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Every morning on Sei's school field, a rooster on the fence handles roll call instead of the teacher, its <radical>mouth</radical> wrapped in a feathery <radical>wrap</radical>. It refuses to crow anyone's number. <radical>One</radical> by one, it screeches the nickname class gave you last week, until the field rings with everyone's most embarrassing <kanji>nickname</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The rooster itself has a name — the groundskeeper calls it <reading>Go</reading>. Every crow comes out as one long 「<reading>ごう</reading>」, stretched over the whole field, until the flag finally goes up and class begins.

items.meaning_mnemonic: The panicking duck yanks again, and a second matching pair of <radical>feathers</radical> pops loose, drifting down to land tip to tip on the pond, mirrored just like the first pair. A fisherman nearby mistakes the twin shapes for a floating insect and casts his line right between them. He reels in nothing but two soaked, stuck-together feathers.
items.reading_mnemonic: The fisherman stares at his soggy catch and groans <reading>ooh</reading>, <reading>う</reading>, disgusted at wasting good bait on nothing but down. He flings the pair back toward the water, where the duck has already forgotten the whole ordeal and gone back to preening at the pond's edge.

items.meaning_mnemonic: At the riverbank the crossing is blocked by one squat, grey <radical>stone</radical> lump, broken off the <radical>mountain</radical> upstream. A small hollow in its face looks like a stone <radical>mouth</radical>. It's planted so solid in the current that the water just splits and foams around it. Immovable, water-stubborn, taking up the whole ford — that lump is a <kanji>boulder</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: A fisherman named <reading>Gan</reading> swings his rod back to cast and cracks it straight into that lump with a flat, ugly thud: <reading>がん</reading>. He stands there rubbing the crack in the wood — the rock doesn't chip.

items.meaning_mnemonic: At the riverbank a single wide plank of <radical>tree</radical>-wood has lain half in the water and half in the mud, propped against a low <radical>cliff</radical> for as long as anyone remembers. It splits down the center with every storm, but villagers' <radical>right hand</radical>s keep dragging it back to lay flat: the only board wide enough to cross on, a <kanji>plank</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Downstream at the same crossing, the chef <reading>Han</reading> — the one who serves every dish split exactly in half — squats over the cracked plank and slices his lunch on it. He mutters 「<reading>はん</reading>」 with each cut: half for him, half for the current.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Two clumps of <radical>grass</radical> push up through the soil in a windowbox. Behind the glass, the <radical>day</radical>'s sun climbs higher, coaxing them taller by noon. The gardener scratches a <radical>ten</radical> mark into the frame, counting the tenth blade to break through — the whole box calls itself grass.
items.reading_mnemonic: The gardener kneels by the windowbox and mutters <reading>そう</reading> under his breath with every seed he plants, like he's saying <reading>sow</reading> to himself out of habit. By the tenth blade, the word is stitched into the dirt.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A stalk of <radical>grain</radical> on the left, beside it the <radical>small</radical> mark — one bristle off the very top, thinnest thing on the plant. Slice an hour the same way and the sliver left in your hand is one <kanji>second</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Byou is the hospital timekeeper with the stopwatch, and she counts out loud in a flat clipped bark — 「<reading>びょう</reading>」, びょう, びょう — one for every tick. She will not speed up and she will not stop. びょう is a single second landing.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Rain floods the school's sports field mid-relay, runners skidding through mud under dripping umbrellas. Then the clouds tear apart, the sky flashing <radical>blue</radical>-green overhead, and one shaft of <radical>sun</radical> lands square on the finish line. Steam lifts off the soaked track — the whole field is suddenly, brightly <kanji>clear up</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: As the sky clears, Sei's hand shoots up first as always, uniform spotless despite the mud. She announces it loud and smug: <reading>せい</reading> — like she's the one who <reading>said</reading> the sky would clear.

items.meaning_mnemonic: At Grandma Kane's shrine the <radical>rain</radical> behind the window freezes mid-fall. Its dashes hang stiff in the glass. Someone drags out the <radical>broom</radical>. Its three bristly prongs sweep the frozen drops into pale drifts over the mossy steps. Even the shrine cats won't leave the bell: it's snow.
items.reading_mnemonic: The groundskeeper everyone calls <reading>Set</reading> mutters <reading>せつ</reading> under his breath every time he has to shovel the steps again. By dawn the drifts are back, deeper than before, and so is his sigh.

items.meaning_mnemonic: On the mountain trail, the vending machine's fan kicks up a strand shed by a passing dog. It hangs in the wind: a flat line at the scalp, hooking into a curl, flicking to a sharp point. It lands stuck to a hiker's sweaty arm, twisting there. That stray curling wisp is <radical>fur</radical>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Back at the vending machine, a hiker named <reading>Moe</reading> picks the stray wisp off his sweaty arm for the third time this climb. He groans <reading>もう</reading>, long and tired, dragging the sound out like his own name stretched thin. Loose fur keeps finding him no matter how high he climbs.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Picture 泳 as one motion at the riverbank: an arm slices forward through the <radical>water</radical>. It flings a trail of <radical>drop</radical>lets out sideways behind it in one clean streak. That arm-cut trailing a spray of droplets is <kanji>swim</kanji> — caught mid-stroke, again and again.
items.reading_mnemonic: At the same riverbank, the lifeguard Ei blows her whistle every single stroke you take, shouting <reading>えい</reading>! — <reading>Ay</reading>! — like she's counting each one out loud. By the tenth lap her voice is the only thing keeping your arms moving.

items.meaning_mnemonic: At the back of Koichi's konbini, a forgotten oil lantern still burns behind the onigiri shelf. Its cap sits crooked, its squat glass body holds the flame steady, and its stubby feet keep it balanced on a crate. All night the glass glows warm <radical>yellow</radical>, fluorescent tubes be damned.
items.reading_mnemonic: Koichi restocks the shelf by lantern light, counting under his breath: <reading>こう</reading>. It comes out low and steady, exactly like a pigeon's <reading>coo</reading>, over and over until every row is full again.

items.meaning_mnemonic: <radical>Rain</radical> streaks down a windowpane. Below the sill, on the <radical>ground</radical>, two chopsticks lie parallel, waiting for a meal — <radical>two</radical>. A silkworm seals itself between them into a <radical>cocoon</radical>, and the drizzle soaks it round, grey, and puffy. That waterlogged cocoon, off the ground, is a cloud.
items.reading_mnemonic: That swollen cocoon keeps drifting away from the ground like a stray <reading>balloon</reading>, and everyone at the window mutters <reading>うん</reading> in surprise as it floats past, still dripping rain.

items.meaning_mnemonic: On the sports field a <radical>bird</radical> lands stiff-legged on the goalpost. Its stick legs clatter against the metal bar. Its beak cracks open into that same perfect square yawn you already know as a <radical>mouth</radical>. It gapes wider than seems possible, and what echoes clear across the field is a piercing chirp.
items.reading_mnemonic: The gym teacher on duty is called <reading>May</reading>. She blows her whistle and shouts <reading>めい</reading> every time that shriek cuts through practice. Nobody on the field mentions that the bird started it.

items.meaning_mnemonic: At Grandma Kane's shrine, an <radical>insect</radical> — a beetle — drops onto the mossy steps. Its whole body writes the shape you are learning: a stiff little head, a long ribbed torso, and a tail curling into one sharp hook. Then it goes still. The shrine cats never even blink. That hooked, segmented outline is one <kanji>bug</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Chuu the loyal mouse trails the beetle across the shrine steps, tiny topknot bobbing, and posts himself over its twitching antenna like an unassigned guard. Every twitch earns one crisp report — <reading>ちゅう</reading> — from the mouse everyone calls <reading>Chuu</reading>, guarding an insect nobody asked him to.

items.meaning_mnemonic: The spool of <radical>thread</radical> teeters on the shelf, one strand trailing loose over the edge. It tips, and three frayed fibers dangling beneath it snag on a nail as it drops. By the time it hits the floor, the whole spool has unraveled into a tangled heap of thread.
items.reading_mnemonic: A seamstress named <reading>Shea</reading> catches the falling spool just before it hits the floor and hisses <reading>し</reading>, a long <reading>shh</reading>, so she doesn't wake the shop cat curled up in the thread bin.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A hiker flicks a coin off the mountain trail. It's on the <radical>slide</radical>, gone before anyone can react. Right at the <radical>ground</radical>, a <radical>barb</radical> flicks up and hooks the coin's edge, yanking it back. Snatching a falling coin like that: pure genius.
items.reading_mnemonic: The hiker introduces himself as <reading>Sai</reading>, showing off his trick over and over. Everyone on the trail starts groaning <reading>さい</reading> before he even throws the coin, tired of his one genius party trick.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A field of grain bows low along the riverbank, each stalk bent double under a head so heavy it can't stand straight. Wind pushes it down further and it still doesn't snap, just dips lower and lower. That endless stooped bow is <radical>barley</radical>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The farmer who tends that field introduces himself as <reading>Baku</reading>, bowing just like his crop. Everyone at the riverbank echoes <reading>ばく</reading> back at him, mimicking his stiff, grain-heavy bow every time he passes.

items.meaning_mnemonic: The <radical>money</radical> clam tips further on its two skinny legs, spilling more coins across the sand. A crow swoops in, snatches every coin in its beak, and hops off — leaving behind an empty, coin-broke shellfish.
items.reading_mnemonic: The coin-thief crow flaps off with a coin in its beak and caws <reading>ばい</reading>, sounding exactly like it's yelling <reading>bye</reading> over its shoulder. That's the reading you shout back at every shellfish it robs.
